key_insight: GAMF-Net improves smartphone skin lesion classification by combining image predictions with grouped clinical information while explicitly tracking missing fields.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support low-cost skin lesion assessment in resource-constrained settings, but clinical utility remains unproven.
method: Groups 10 clinical variables into demographics, history-related risk, and lesion presentation.
Encodes values and availability masks; each group adds image-conditioned evidence to image-based predictions.
Equally weights available groups and reverts exactly to image-only predictions when all clinical information is missing.
evidence_signal: On PAD-UFES-20 with patient-disjoint five-fold evaluation and separate training, validation, and test partitions, GAMF-Net achieved 74.17±2.85% accuracy and 70.11±2.11% balanced accuracy, exceeding the strongest reimplemented baseline by 2.37 and 2.59 percentage points, respectively.
watch_item: Evaluation was limited to one dataset; performance across external populations, smartphone devices, and real-world missing-data patterns remains uncertain.
paper_title: GAMF-Net: Grouped Availability-Aware Multimodal Fusion for Smartphone Skin Lesion Classification
